title: Gluten-Free Apple Cinnamon Crumble Cupcakes
shortDescription: Tender gluten-free apple cupcakes with a cinnamon swirl frosting and crumble topping, ready in about 55 minutes.
description: These cupcakes taste like apple crumble in cake form. I tested this recipe in my home kitchen after one too many failed gluten-free apple bakes that turned gummy. The trick is grating the apple fine and squeezing out extra juice before it hits the batter The cake stays soft and moist. Packed with real apple pieces and warm cinnamon. A swirl of cinnamon buttercream goes on top, then a crunchy gluten-free oat crumble finishes each cupcake. This recipe works well for fall parties or a cozy weekend bake. It uses a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend, so no special substitutions are needed. Make the crumble a day ahead if you want to save time on baking day. It keeps well in an airtight container at room temperature.
ingredients: 1 3/4 cups gluten-free 1:1 baking flour blend (with xanthan gum)
1 cup peeled, finely grated apple, liquid squeezed out (about 1 medium apple)
1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
1/2 cup gluten-free rolled oats, for crumble
1/4 cup gluten-free 1:1 flour blend, for crumble
3 tbsp cold unsalted butter, cubed, for crumble
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.

Make the crumble first. Mix oats, flour, brown sugar, and cinnamon in a small bowl. Cut in cold butter with your fingers until it looks like wet sand. Spread on a plate and chill while you make the cake.
Whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt in a bowl. Set aside.
Beat softened butter and brown sugar together for 2 minutes until fluffy. Add eggs one at a time, then mix in vanilla.
Add the dry mix in three parts, alternating with buttermilk. Mix on low speed just until combined.
Fold in the grated apple by hand. Do not overmix, or the cupcakes will turn dense.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two thirds full. Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan for 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool completely before frosting.
Make the frosting. Beat butter until smooth, then add powdered sugar, cinnamon, and heavy cream. Beat 3 minutes until light and fluffy.
Pipe frosting on cooled cupcakes in a tall swirl. Press crumble onto the top of each cupcake before serving.
tips: Squeeze grated apple in a paper towel before adding it to the batter. Extra moisture makes gluten-free cake gummy.
Chill the crumble mix for 10 minutes before baking it separately at 325°F for 10 minutes, if you want extra crunch.
Room temperature eggs and butter blend smoother and give a more even crumb.
Store leftover cupcakes in the fridge for up to 4 days. Bring to room temperature before serving.

faq.question: Can I use apple sauce instead of grated apple?
faq.answer: Grated apple works better here. Apple sauce adds too much moisture and can make the gluten-free cake dense.

faq.question: Which gluten-free flour blend works best for this recipe?
faq.answer: Use a 1:1 baking blend that already contains xanthan gum. I tested this with a cup-for-cup blend and got a soft, even crumb.

faq.question: Can I make the crumble ahead of time?
faq.answer: Yes. Bake the crumble a day ahead and store it in an airtight container at room temperature until you frost the cupcakes.

faq.question: Why did my cupcakes sink in the middle?
faq.answer: This usually means the apple was too wet or the pan was opened too early. Squeeze the apple well and wait until the last few minutes to check doneness.

conclusion: These apple cinnamon cupcakes bring fall flavor without any gluten. The soft cake, cinnamon frosting, and crunchy crumble make a treat worth repeating every season.
